entries.title: Evening Briefing · 21 November 2026
headlines: Tankers hit near the Strait of Hormuz as Iran blames sea mines; who fired is unverified
NATO vows to defend every inch of Poland after Russian missiles land on Polish soil
Bennett backs an Eisenkot-led unity government in Israel; Likud talks begin Sunday
Modi opens the Nitish Setu bridge over the Ganga and launches Rs 34,470 crore of projects
England beat the All Blacks 37-12 and Leeds win 4-1 at Chelsea

stories.headline: Tankers struck near Khasab as Iran blames sea mines
stories.summary: UKMTO reported two incidents on Saturday: an outbound tanker hit on the stern by an unidentified projectile about 11 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman, and a tanker hit in the engine room 17nm east of the port, with no casualties reported. Iran's navy says a tanker that caught fire on Friday hit a naval mine, and the IRGC claims to have downed two US drones, which the US has not confirmed.
stories.whyItMatters: Before the war, nearly a fifth of the world's crude passed through the strait, so shipping attacks there are the main risk to oil prices and freight costs.

stories.headline: Russian missiles land in Poland; NATO chief visits Warsaw
stories.summary: During Russia's overnight attack on Ukraine, two missiles and a jet-powered drone came down in south-east Poland, injuring no one. Donald Tusk called it an intentional provocation. On Saturday Mark Rutte said in Warsaw that NATO will defend all of Poland's territory, and the North Atlantic Council meets on Monday.
stories.whyItMatters: It is the most serious breach of NATO airspace in the war so far, a day after the Shenzhen declaration promised strategic stability.

stories.headline: Drones hit a Russian cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland
stories.summary: Two drones struck the Kaliningrad-bound cargo ship Sparta II in international waters west of Gogland island on Saturday morning, starting a fire on board. Finland restricted air and sea traffic in the eastern gulf. No one has claimed the attack.
stories.whyItMatters: The war is reaching into the Baltic, right on NATO's border, so the risk of an incident involving alliance members is rising.

stories.headline: Three Houthi missiles aimed at Riyadh are intercepted
stories.summary: The Saudi-led coalition says it shot down three ballistic missiles fired at the Saudi capital early on Saturday, as well as a drone heading for the south. No casualties were reported. Two days earlier a Houthi strike damaged the Public Investment Fund tower in Riyadh.
stories.whyItMatters: Saudi Arabia is being drawn directly into the wider Iran conflict, which puts Gulf aviation and Red Sea ports at risk.

stories.headline: Israel: Bennett backs Eisenkot for a unity government
stories.summary: On Saturday evening Naftali Bennett endorsed a broad government led by Gadi Eisenkot and said he would not sit with Netanyahu under any circumstances. Eisenkot's Yashar party has invited Likud to marathon coalition talks starting Sunday, with 29 days left on his mandate.
stories.whyItMatters: Netanyahu's way back to power is getting narrower. If no deal is reached, the fallback is a minority government.

stories.headline: Shenzhen declaration: Ukraine clause reportedly cut at US request
stories.summary: Finland's President Alexander Stubb said in Berlin that a passage on Ukraine was removed from the Trump-Xi-Putin text because Washington asked for it. In Kryvyi Rih, the number injured in Friday's attack has risen to 60, and two people were killed.
stories.whyItMatters: European leaders worry that big-power deals are being made without Kyiv. The account comes from Stubb and the US has not confirmed it.

stories.headline: Barnham votes 257-16 in symbolic leave-the-UK ballot
stories.summary: Residents of the Suffolk village held a non-binding vote on Saturday to protest Home Office plans to house up to 931 single men seeking asylum at the former RAF Barnham site. A 3.4 million pound design contract has been awarded, but no final decision has been taken.
stories.whyItMatters: Plans for large asylum sites are turning into local flashpoints, and Reform UK is using them in its campaigning.

stories.headline: SNP would keep Burnham in No 10 in a hung parliament, report says
stories.summary: ITV Border, citing unnamed sources, reports that the SNP leadership would vote to keep Andy Burnham as prime minister after the next election without upfront demands, then use confidence-and-supply leverage to press for a second independence referendum. Burnham has ruled out a second referendum.
stories.whyItMatters: The report suggests parties are already planning for a hung parliament and the deals that would follow.

stories.headline: Independent review ordered into NHS Grampian surgery deaths
stories.summary: Scotland's Health Secretary Angela Constance ordered an independent review of liver and pancreatic surgery at NHS Grampian, after a 2022 whistleblower report found 19 of 31 deaths avoidable. She will make a statement to Holyrood on Tuesday.
stories.whyItMatters: It is a serious patient-safety case, and it raises questions about how the Scottish government dealt with the warnings.

stories.headline: Yellow rain warning for Devon and Cornwall on Sunday
stories.summary: The Met Office warning runs from 06:00 to 23:59 on Sunday, with 20 to 40mm of rain widely, 60 to 80mm in parts of south Devon and Cornwall, and possibly more than 100mm on Dartmoor.
stories.whyItMatters: Flooding, travel disruption and power cuts are possible in the south-west.

stories.headline: Modi opens Nitish Setu and launches Rs 34,470 crore of projects
stories.summary: In Vaishali, the Prime Minister opened the six-lane Kachchi Dargah to Bidupur bridge over the Ganga, named Nitish Setu after the former chief minister, which runs 9.76km over the river and took about 14 years to build. He also announced a Rs 6,000 crore steel project in Gaya and flagged off 100 electric buses.
stories.whyItMatters: It is a showcase project for the NDA government in Bihar. The RJD has called the naming an insult, and the claim that it is India's longest river bridge has not been officially confirmed.

stories.headline: Manipur toxic liquor deaths rise to 16
stories.summary: The toll, given as 11 this morning, is now 16: nine in Chandel district and seven in Kakching. Outlets give between 370 and 600 people treated in hospital, six people have been arrested, and a state committee has a month to report.
stories.whyItMatters: It is one of the worst hooch tragedies in the north-east in years, and the toll may rise further.

stories.headline: Ladakh holds first local polls since becoming a Union Territory
stories.summary: Turnout was about 70 percent for sarpanch seats and 52 percent in municipal wards in Leh and Kargil, in the first grassroots elections since 2019. The Leh Apex Body has been on hunger strike since 12 November, demanding that the 4 December hill council polls be postponed.
stories.whyItMatters: The turnout is a test of public engagement in Ladakh amid local demands for constitutional safeguards.

stories.headline: India to host WorldSkills Asia 2027 in Greater Noida
stories.summary: Speaking at a skills convocation in Lucknow, Modi announced the event and highlighted Rs 60,000 crore under the PM-SETU scheme to upgrade ITIs, with new trades including AI, drones and green hydrogen.
stories.whyItMatters: The skills drive is central to India's jobs strategy, and the announcement came in Uttar Pradesh ahead of its 2027 election.

stories.headline: Cyclone Akvan passes Odisha without loss of life
stories.summary: Akvan crossed the coast near Gopalpur on Friday with winds of 70 to 80km/h after about 3.7 lakh people were evacuated. On Saturday the state said there were no deaths and promised input subsidies to farmers whose paddy was damaged.
stories.whyItMatters: Early evacuation worked, but it was Odisha's third cyclone threat in under a month and the harvest has been hit.

stories.headline: No new Immigration Rules today
stories.summary: No new Statement of Changes has appeared since this morning; the latest remains HC 584 of 3 September. Its rise in student maintenance funds (to 1,570 pounds a month in London and 1,203 pounds elsewhere) applies to applications made on or after 30 November. The GOV.UK collection page could not be loaded on this run, so the check relied on GOV.UK search results.
stories.whyItMatters: Skilled Worker, settlement and fee rules are unchanged as of tonight.

stories.headline: Earned settlement: policy set, but rules not yet laid
stories.summary: The Home Office's 2 November plan raises the standard qualifying period for ILR from five to ten years, with shorter routes planned for higher earners and some public-service roles. GOV.UK gives no start date. Law firms expect the rules to start appearing in a December Statement of Changes.
stories.whyItMatters: The plan has no general protection for people already in the UK, so Indian Skilled Workers earning below about 50,271 pounds could face a ten-year wait.

stories.headline: Migration Advisory Committee reviews talent visas
stories.summary: The MAC's Talent Routes Review, published on 17 November, says Global Talent broadly works. It suggests an income test and evidence of continued activity in the applicant's field at settlement, and recommends abolishing or overhauling Innovator Founder. The government has not responded.
stories.whyItMatters: These are recommendations only. A separate MAC report will decide whether Skilled Workers can use the fastest three-year settlement route.

stories.headline: Wellington Test: India lead by 118 going into day four
stories.summary: India are 486/4 in reply to New Zealand's 368, after KL Rahul's 136 and Shubman Gill's 98, with Rishabh Pant unbeaten on 55. Day four starts at about 22:00 GMT tonight.
stories.whyItMatters: India can push for a big lead and try to force a result on a slow pitch. New Zealand are likely to bat for a draw.

stories.headline: Leeds win 4-1 at Chelsea
stories.summary: Noah Okafor scored twice and Calvert-Lewin and Aaronson added goals as Leeds came from behind for their first league win at Stamford Bridge since 1999. In other 15:00 games, Spurs beat Ipswich 2-0, Bournemouth beat Forest 2-0, Coventry beat Palace 3-2, and Villa and Sunderland drew 0-0.
stories.whyItMatters: Leeds move up to sixth. The defeat adds pressure on Xabi Alonso at Chelsea.

stories.headline: Man City held 1-1 by Fulham
stories.summary: Rodrigo Muniz put Fulham ahead and Elliot Anderson equalised for City, while Haaland had a goal ruled out after a review. The draw ends City's run of 20 straight wins over Fulham, which began in 2012.
stories.whyItMatters: City have now gone four league games without a win, which helps leaders Arsenal.

stories.headline: Newcastle v Arsenal: Arsenal led 1-0 at half-time
stories.summary: Eberechi Eze scored on 33 minutes from a Kai Havertz pass at St James' Park. The second half was under way when this briefing was written, and the final score is not included.
stories.whyItMatters: A win would put the leaders, already on 27 points, further clear of City.

stories.headline: England beat New Zealand 37-12; Ireland edge South Africa
stories.summary: England scored five tries at Twickenham for their first back-to-back wins over the All Blacks since 2002. In Dublin, Ireland beat South Africa 20-17, with two tries from Robert Baloucoune.
stories.whyItMatters: England go top of the northern table, depending on France v Argentina tonight.

stories.headline: F1: Verstappen on pole in Las Vegas
stories.summary: Kimi Antonelli was fastest in qualifying but takes a five-place engine penalty, so Max Verstappen starts first ahead of George Russell and Lando Norris. The race runs overnight UK time.

stories.headline: Cargo Dragon due to splash down at about 21:55 GMT
stories.summary: SpaceX's CRS-35 capsule left the space station on Friday and is due to land off California tonight, carrying research samples that include a 3D-bioprinted blood vessel. NASA is not streaming the splashdown.

stories.headline: ISRO targets December for first uncrewed Gaganyaan flight
stories.summary: ISRO chairman V Narayanan says the G1 mission will fly in December on a human-rated LVM3, carrying the humanoid robot Vyommitra, with the first crewed flight aimed for early 2027. No launch date has been announced.
stories.whyItMatters: It is the last big step before India's first human spaceflight, and the mission has already slipped twice.

stories.headline: China's Shenzhou-24 may carry a Pakistani astronaut
stories.summary: The rocket has been rolled out at Jiuquan, and observers expect launch on 25 November with the first foreign astronaut to visit China's Tiangong station. China has not officially named the date or the crew.
stories.whyItMatters: It would be a China-Pakistan milestone, and it will be watched closely in India while Gaganyaan waits.

stories.headline: Wall Street ends a brutal week in correction
stories.summary: Friday 20 Nov close (16:00 ET), markets closed today: S&P 500 down 3.70 percent at 6,910.39 (down 8.6 percent on the week), Dow down 1.93 percent at 48,147.33 (down 8.0 percent), Nasdaq Composite down 5.28 percent at 22,617.73 (down 10.0 percent). Nvidia fell 14 percent on a Reuters report of an SEC accounting review, leaving it down 23 percent on the week, and Fed minutes leaned toward rate rises.
stories.whyItMatters: The AI trade that drove this year's gains is unwinding quickly. Monday's open will show whether the selling is slowing.

stories.headline: FTSE 100 falls 5.1 percent over the week
stories.summary: Friday 20 Nov close (16:35 GMT): FTSE 100 down 1.02 percent at 10,346.34, its fifth straight fall. Tech-linked names such as Polar Capital Technology and Halma fell hardest, while defensive stocks such as Unilever rose.
stories.whyItMatters: The global tech sell-off is hitting UK pensions and ISAs, even though London holds relatively few tech shares.

stories.headline: Sensex and Nifty at nine-month highs as funds rotate to India
stories.summary: Friday 20 Nov close (15:30 IST): Sensex up 1.08 percent at 83,919.71 and Nifty 50 up 1.12 percent at 25,800.60, led by banks. Investors moved money out of AI stocks and into India, and foreign buyers have bought more than 12 billion dollars of Indian equities this month.
stories.whyItMatters: India is acting as a refuge from the AI sell-off, which is good for Indian funds and helps the rupee.

stories.headline: Bitcoin drops to about 55,300 dollars overnight, then rebounds
stories.summary: The cryptocurrency hit its lowest level since September 2024 as about 2.7 billion dollars of leveraged bets were wiped out in a day. It has since climbed back above 60,000 dollars.
stories.whyItMatters: Crypto trades over the weekend, so it gives the first read on risk appetite before stock markets reopen on Monday.

entries.title: Morning Briefing · 21 November 2026
headlines: Wall Street's worst day in years: S&P 500 down 3.70 percent, Nasdaq down 5.28 percent, with the S&P and Dow in correction
Nvidia sinks 14 percent on a report the SEC is examining its accounting
UK-EU reset deal: food checks to go from 2028, tuition fees still unresolved
India lead New Zealand by 118 at 486/4 after Rahul's 136 and Gill's 98
Russian strike on Kryvyi Rih kills two and injures 52

stories.headline: Kryvyi Rih: missile strike, then drones on rescuers
stories.summary: A Russian missile hit Kryvyi Rih on Friday evening, killing a 7-year-old boy and a 20-year-old emergency medic and injuring 52. Police say two drone attacks followed on the rescue effort, and overnight drones injured 11 in a Kharkiv-region apartment block.
stories.whyItMatters: The repeated strikes on rescue crews and energy sites come a day after the attack on Kyiv's bridges, with no ceasefire talks in sight.

stories.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin sign a short peace declaration in Shenzhen
stories.summary: Meeting at the APEC summit on Thursday, the three leaders committed to strategic stability, restated that a nuclear war cannot be won, and pledged steady energy supplies. Reports say the text does not deal directly with Ukraine or Iran.
stories.whyItMatters: It is the first three-way statement of its kind, but it leaves the two live wars untouched.

stories.headline: Iran: reports of new US-Israeli strike planning
stories.summary: Unnamed sources quoted by CBS, the New York Times and Axios say Washington and Israel are weighing a fresh air campaign, even as Trump says he is in no rush. The Senate rejected a war powers resolution 48 to 51 on Thursday, and Iran denies Trump's chemical and biological weapons claim.
stories.whyItMatters: Mixed signals from Washington keep oil and shipping risk high; Brent ended Friday near 92.6 dollars.

stories.headline: What is in the UK-EU reset deal, and when
stories.summary: A common food and plant-health area removing most border checks is aimed for 1 March 2028, and linked carbon markets also target 2028. Full treaty texts have not been published and the dates are targets pending ratification.
stories.whyItMatters: Exporters and food importers gain a timetable, but nothing changes at the border for more than two years.

stories.headline: Tuition fees: a six-month deadline, and the opposition attacks
stories.summary: The EU wants its students charged home fees in England; Britain has offered only significantly reduced fees, and a six-month deadline has been set. Burnham says the package adds about 0.5 percent to GDP; Kemi Badenoch questioned the figure and Nigel Farage said it breaks Labour's single market pledge.
stories.whyItMatters: The fees row could delay parts of the deal before the youth scheme bill arrives next week.

stories.headline: Core sector growth hits a record 10.9 percent in October
stories.summary: Output in India's eight core infrastructure industries rose 10.9 percent from a year earlier, the highest in the series, helped by an infrastructure push and a weak base.
stories.whyItMatters: It supports the case for strong growth this quarter, while retail inflation sits above the RBI's tolerance band.

stories.headline: Supreme Court dismisses Tamil Nadu's Cauvery plea
stories.summary: The court rejected Tamil Nadu's petition in its long-running water-sharing dispute with Karnataka.
stories.whyItMatters: Cauvery water is a recurring political flashpoint between the two states.

stories.headline: Spurious liquor kills 11 in Manipur
stories.summary: Eleven people have died and more than 300 have been taken to hospital after drinking toxic liquor, according to early reports.
stories.whyItMatters: The toll may rise, and the case is likely to put pressure on the state's liquor enforcement.

stories.headline: Modi in Bihar to launch 34,470 crore rupees of projects
stories.summary: The Prime Minister is due in Vaishali today to open development projects, including a bridge over the Ganga. Nepal's PM Balendra Shah arrives in Delhi tomorrow.
stories.whyItMatters: The projects focus on transport links in north Bihar.

stories.headline: No new Immigration Rules overnight
stories.summary: No new Statement of Changes has been found; the latest remains HC 584 of 3 September. Earned settlement is still announced policy only, with no rules laid and no start date, so current settlement rules still apply to Skilled Worker visa holders.
stories.whyItMatters: Indian nationals planning ILR can still apply under today's rules; watch for a new Statement of Changes.

stories.headline: Student maintenance amounts rise on 30 November
stories.summary: Under HC 584, the monthly maintenance funds students must show rise from 1,529 to 1,570 pounds and from 1,171 to 1,203 pounds for applications made on or after 30 November. An EU Settlement Scheme identity-document change follows on 9 December.
stories.whyItMatters: Students applying in the next fortnight should check which amount applies to their application date.

stories.headline: Rahul's century puts India 118 ahead in Wellington
stories.summary: India reached 486/4 at stumps on day three, replying to New Zealand's 368. KL Rahul made 136, his 13th Test hundred, and Shubman Gill was out for 98. Day four starts overnight UK time.
stories.whyItMatters: With a big lead and two days left, India have the chance to win the first Test.

stories.headline: Premier League: leaders Arsenal at Newcastle
stories.summary: Arsenal, on 27 points from 10 games, visit Newcastle at 17:30 GMT today, and Manchester City host Fulham at 12:30. Liverpool v Manchester United, Pochettino's first game, is on Sunday at 16:30, with United 18th.
stories.whyItMatters: An Arsenal win would stretch the lead to eight points before Brighton play on Sunday.

stories.headline: Cargo Dragon heads for splashdown tonight
stories.summary: SpaceX's uncrewed cargo Dragon left the space station at 17:05 GMT on Friday. NASA expects splashdown off California at about 21:55 GMT tonight, without a live stream.
stories.whyItMatters: The capsule brings back science samples from the station.

stories.headline: Wall Street: S&P and Dow in correction, Nasdaq negative for the year
stories.summary: Friday 20 Nov close (16:00 ET): S&P 500 down 3.70 percent at 6,910.39, Dow down 1.93 percent at 48,147.33, Nasdaq Composite down 5.28 percent at 22,617.73. Tech fell about 7 percent and the VIX closed near 36.
stories.whyItMatters: Investors are doubting that AI spending will pay off, and hawkish Fed comments added to the selling.

stories.headline: Nvidia down 14 percent on SEC report; Anthropic slips again
stories.summary: Nvidia fell about 14 percent after Reuters reported that SEC enforcement staff are looking at possible accounting issues. Broadcom, AMD and Micron fell 12 to 14 percent, and Anthropic closed near 88.90 dollars, down 8.5 percent but above its 83 dollar IPO price.
stories.whyItMatters: Nvidia has lost almost half its value since its October record and carries the most weight in the AI trade.

stories.headline: FTSE 100 ends a fifth losing day
stories.summary: The FTSE 100 closed Friday (16:35 GMT) down 1.02 percent at 10,346.34 as tech-linked names slid and miners and banks weighed, while defensive stocks rose.
stories.whyItMatters: The fall came before Wall Street's late slide, so London may open lower on Monday.

stories.headline: Sensex and Nifty buck the trend at nine-month highs
stories.summary: Friday close (15:30 IST): Sensex up 1.08 percent at 83,919.71 and Nifty 50 up 1.12 percent at 25,800.60, led by Axis Bank, HDFC Bank and Apollo Hospitals. Markets are closed today.
stories.whyItMatters: Friday's US rout is a test for Monday's open at 09:15 IST.
